> **Responsive Layout Pattern** — Architectural pattern for mobile-first responsive layouts in enterprise React applications. Defines the viewport tier system, container strategy, layout model (CSS Grid / Flexbox), and the WCAG 2.5.8 touch target requirement. For Tailwind CSS / React implementation steps, see [GUID-APP-UI-002](../../../strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md).

[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without a shared responsive layout pattern, micro-frontend teams independently invent breakpoints, container widths, and grid systems. The result is modules that behave correctly in isolation but produce inconsistent or broken layouts when composed into a shell portal across varying viewport sizes.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The Responsive Layout Pattern defines four structural decisions that all React layouts must follow:

1. **Viewport tier system** — six named breakpoints (mobile through 2xl) as the single source of truth
2. **Container strategy** — four named container variants (default, narrow, wide, fluid) with defined max-widths
3. **Layout model** — CSS Grid for page-level structure; Flexbox for component-level alignment
4. **Mobile accessibility floor** — minimum 44×44px touch targets on all interactive elements (WCAG 2.5.8)
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#when-to-use-this-pattern]

### When to Use This Pattern

- Designing or reviewing any page layout in a React application (shell or remote module)
- Establishing layout acceptance criteria for a new micro-frontend module
- Evaluating an existing application's responsive behaviour against enterprise standards
- Defining the layout layer during application architecture review
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Composition consistency**: Modules built on the same breakpoint system compose predictably inside any shell
- **Mobile-first by default**: The pattern enforces progressive enhancement — base styles target the smallest viewport
- **Accessible on all devices**: Touch target and orientation requirements are built into the acceptance criteria
- **Token alignment**: Container max-widths and spacing are drawn from the enterprise design token system (GUID-APP-UI-001)

page_texts.9:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell healthcare applications serve users on a wide range of devices — from mobile phones used by field case managers to large-monitor workstations in clinical and administrative settings. Applications are delivered as Module Federation micro-frontends composed into shell portals. A module that renders correctly in isolation but breaks the shell layout on a different viewport creates a poor user experience and increases support cost.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The enterprise UI stack ([ADR-APP-003](../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md)) uses Tailwind CSS, which provides a mobile-first utility class system. The design token system ([GUID-APP-UI-001](../../../strategy/guidance/application/design-tokens/GUID-APP-UI-001-design-tokens-theming-guidance.md)) defines custom container widths and spacing values that this pattern references.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without this pattern:

- Remote modules use hard-coded pixel widths that break in shell application layouts
- Teams implement incompatible grid systems (Bootstrap, CSS Grid, Flexbox-only) that do not compose
- Breakpoints differ across modules — a "large" screen in one module is a "medium" screen in another
- Touch targets on mobile are undersized, failing WCAG 2.5.8

---
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#decision-1-viewport-tier-system]

### Decision 1: Viewport Tier System

Six named viewport tiers are the single enterprise source of truth for breakpoint values. All responsive layout decisions reference only these tiers — never raw pixel values.

| Tier        | Minimum Width | Target Device Context               |
| ----------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| (default)   | 0px           | Mobile phones (portrait)            |
| Small        | 640px         | Mobile phones (landscape) / tablets |
| Medium       | 768px         | Tablets                             |
| Large        | 1024px        | Laptops / small desktops            |
| Extra-large  | 1280px        | Desktop workstations                |
| 2xl          | 1536px        | Large / wide monitors               |

**Mobile-first rule**: All styles default to the smallest viewport. Larger viewport overrides are applied progressively at each tier.
page_texts.14:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#decision-2-container-strategy]

### Decision 2: Container Strategy

Four named container variants cover all content width requirements. Teams select the appropriate variant for their content type; they do not invent ad-hoc max-widths.

| Variant   | Max Width  | Use Case                                           |
| --------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | 1280px     | Standard portal page content                       |
| `narrow`  | 672px      | Forms, articles, single-column reading content     |
| `wide`    | 1536px     | Data-heavy dashboards, wide data grids             |
| `fluid`   | None       | Full-bleed sections (hero banners, full-width maps)|

All container variants are horizontally centred with consistent responsive horizontal padding.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#decision-3-layout-model]

### Decision 3: Layout Model

Two layout mechanisms are used at distinct levels of the component hierarchy:

| Mechanism  | Where used                          | Purpose                                      |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| CSS Grid   | Page-level and section-level layout | Multi-column structure; 12-column base grid  |
| Flexbox    | Component-level alignment           | Button groups, icon+label pairs, card headers|

CSS Grid governs how regions of a page relate to each other. Flexbox governs how elements within a component align to each other. The two are not interchangeable.

**12-column base grid**: Page-level grids use a 12-column system. On mobile, all columns span the full width. Progressive enhancement assigns partial column spans at `md:` and `lg:` tiers. Column counts scale: 4 at base, 8 at `md`, 12 at `lg`.
page_texts.16:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#decision-4-mobile-accessibility-floor]

### Decision 4: Mobile Accessibility Floor

All interactive elements must meet the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum touch target size of 24×24px. The enterprise target is 44×44px (Apple/Google HIG recommendation).

- Inline buttons: `min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px]`
- Icon-only buttons: must also carry an accessible label in addition to meeting size requirements
- Tables with row actions on mobile: row actions must be touch-sized

page_texts.17:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#pattern-structure]

## Pattern Structure

```
Responsive Layout
├── Viewport Tier System
│   ├── default (0px)   — mobile portrait base
│   ├── sm (640px)      — mobile landscape / tablet
│   ├── md (768px)      — tablet
│   ├── lg (1024px)     — laptop / small desktop
│   ├── xl (1280px)     — desktop workstation
│   └── 2xl (1536px)   — large / wide monitor
│
├── Container Strategy
│   ├── default  — max-w 1280px, centred, responsive padding
│   ├── narrow   — max-w 672px,  centred, responsive padding
│   ├── wide     — max-w 1536px, centred, responsive padding
│   └── fluid    — full width,   responsive padding only
│
├── Layout Model
│   ├── CSS Grid (page / section level)
│   │   ├── 4 cols at base → 8 cols at md → 12 cols at lg
│   │   └── Col spans assigned per viewport tier
│   └── Flexbox (component level)
│       ├── Alignment of sub-elements within a component
│       └── Stack → row progressive enhancement
│
└── Mobile Accessibility Floor
    ├── Touch target minimum: 44×44px on all interactive elements
    ├── Tables: scrollable wrapper on mobile; priority columns hidden below threshold
    └── Navigation: hamburger / bottom bar on mobile → sidebar at lg
```

page_texts.20:
[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#acceptance-criteria]

### Acceptance Criteria

A layout satisfies this pattern when:

- [ ] All viewport breakpoints use the six named tiers — no raw pixel media queries
- [ ] All page regions use one of the four named container variants
- [ ] Page-level multi-column structure uses CSS Grid; component-level alignment uses Flexbox
- [ ] Base styles (no prefix) target mobile; larger viewports progressively enhance
- [ ] All interactive elements meet a minimum 44×44px touch target
- [ ] Tables on mobile are wrapped in a horizontally scrollable container
- [ ] Navigation collapses to hamburger or bottom bar below `lg:` breakpoint
- [ ] Layout tested at 375px (mobile), 768px (tablet), and 1280px (desktop) viewports

[patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-002-responsive-layout-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

1. Use exactly the six named viewport tiers — never invent raw pixel breakpoints
2. Wrap all page content in one of the four named container variants
3. CSS Grid for page structure; Flexbox for component-level alignment
4. Base styles = mobile; progressively enhance with `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`, `2xl:`
5. All interactive elements need a minimum 44×44px touch target
6. For Tailwind/React implementation, see [GUID-APP-UI-002](../../../strategy/guidance/application/responsive-layout/GUID-APP-UI-002-responsive-layout-implementation-guidance.md)
